analysis.investment_thesis: eClerx is a recovering KPO/BPO mid-cap with strong recent momentum — revenue nearly doubled in 4 years at 21% CAGR — but a decade of weak earnings growth (5.2% CAGR) and a trailing PEG of ~1.3 make it a "wait for a better price" story rather than a screaming buy. The forward PEG of ~0.9 (implying ~21% forward earnings growth) is intriguing but needs sustained execution to warrant conviction.
key_strengths: Excellent capital efficiency: ROCE of 28% and ROE of 22.8% with very low D/E of 0.15 — a clean, cash-generative business
Strong recent acceleration: revenue grew 1,564→3,366 Cr (2021–2025, 21% CAGR) with FCF surging from 326 to 539 Cr in 4 years
High promoter conviction at 54.53% holding with DII backing at 23.8% — management owns the story
key_risks: Decade-long stagnation (2016–2021): net profit declined from 342 Cr to 209 Cr — raises serious questions about cyclicality and whether this is a true grower or a lumpy cyclical
Trailing PEG ~1.3 leaves little room for error; if earnings growth reverts toward the 9Y CAGR of 5%, the stock is expensive at P/E 22.9x
Operating margin compression over the full cycle: operating income CAGR of just 5.9% vs revenue CAGR of 11% signals margins have been squeezed — current 21.5% operating margin needs to hold
red_flags: Net profit CAGR of only 5.2% over 9 years — not the 15%+ earnings growth Lynch wants to see in a fast grower
Finance costs compounding at 48.9% CAGR (1 Cr in 2016 → 36 Cr in 2025) — borrowings creeping up to 395 Cr even as the business generates strong FCF
The 2016–2020 earnings decline followed by recovery looks cyclical, not structural — hard to call this a reliable compounder
analysis.detailed_analysis:
eClerx is a niche B2B KPO player serving global financial services, retail, and telecom clients — not the kind of consumer-observable business Lynch loves, but the numbers tell an improving story. The last 4 years are genuinely impressive: revenue nearly doubled (1,564→3,366 Cr), FCF grew 65% (326→539 Cr), and the balance sheet remains lean (D/E 0.15, net cash positive with 542 Cr cash vs 395 Cr borrowings). ROCE of 28% is best-in-class for mid-cap IT services. But Lynch's first question is always "what's the story?" — and here the story is complicated by a brutal 2016–2020 period where profits fell 39% (342→209 Cr). That's not a fast grower's track record; that's a turnaround or cyclical.

The valuation math is borderline. Trailing PEG = 22.9 / 17.6 (5Y earnings CAGR) = ~1.30 — above Lynch's preferred 1.0 threshold. Forward PEG drops to ~0.90 if you believe 21% forward earnings growth implied by the Forward P/E of 18.93, which is more interesting. For Lynch, this slots as a recovering stalwart that has re-accelerated, not a classic fast grower. At current prices, you're paying a fair but not exciting multiple for a business that needs to prove the 2021–2025 growth rate was structural and not just post-COVID catch-up plus currency tailwinds. Worth watching, not chasing.
